newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends down on harvest, ahead of crop data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends down on harvest, ahead of crop data.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on harvest pressure but trading was quiet on positioning before the release at 0730 CDT Friday of USDA's crop production and supply/demand reports, traders said.
"Just evening up ahead of Friday. We drifted all day and looking for direction," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
An average of analysts' estimates placed 1996 U.S. corn production at 8.951 billion bushels, up from USDA's forecast in September for 8.804 billion and well above 1995 production of 7.374 billion.

Traders said active harvesting of the U.S. corn crop may have lent pressure to prices but slow farmer selling and mostly firm basis values underpinned prices as did some reports of lower corn yields as the U.S. harvest advanced.
However, in the western Corn Belt, especially in Nebraska, there have been indications of excellent per acre yields.
The first leg of a corn tour through Nebraska ended Tuesday with participants saying the average potential yield was running above average in the seven counties visited.
Corn futures closed unchanged to 3-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 2-3/4 at $2.93-3/4 a bushel.
Traders agreed the corn market remains in a seasonal slump despite conflicting ideas about yield reports from early harvested fields.
"We're hearing mixed results on yields but we do know the farmer is not selling," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
The slow farmer selling helped underpin corn futures as did signals the market remains oversold despite price rises early this week.
The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for December closed at 30.428 points. An RSI of 30 or less is generally considered oversold and 20 or less is usually seen as very oversold.

Key players included ADM Investor Services with two million bushels sold in the December and R.J. O'Brien sold two million December, traders said. Prudential Securities bought three million bushels of March, sources said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 45,000 contracts, down from 52,908 Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
Corn options featured Rosenthal Collins' purchase of 650 December $3.10 puts at 17 to 19-1/2 cents and Prudential Securities bought 500 July $3.50 calls at 8-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, down from 21,190 Tuesday.
